title: pdf
summary: Evaluate a fitted or named probability distribution density or probability mass function.

gpu_support.notes: The CPU evaluator preserves single output precision and restores fallback results to the owning provider when its precision can represent the result; explicit gpuArray input fails rather than silently returning a host result when restoration is impossible.

description: `pdf(pd,x)` evaluates the density or probability mass function for a `ProbabilityDistribution` object returned by `fitdist`. `pdf(distname,x,params...)` evaluates supported named distributions directly.
behaviors: `pd` must be a fitted distribution object returned by `fitdist`, or `distname` must name a supported distribution.
Supported named distributions are `"Normal"`, `"Exponential"`, `"Lognormal"`, `"Gamma"`, `"Weibull"`, and `"Poisson"` with their standard scalar parameters.
`x` and named-distribution parameters may be scalar or mutually broadcast-compatible numeric arrays; the output has their broadcast shape.
Typed-integer evaluation points and distribution parameters are independent RunMat extensions and reject values that cannot cross the binary64 probability boundary exactly.
Continuous distributions return probability densities. Poisson returns probability mass values at integer support points and zero outside the support.

faqs.question: Can pdf evaluate by distribution name?
faqs.answer: Yes. The named overload supports normal, exponential, lognormal, gamma, Weibull, and Poisson with scalar parameters. Distribution-specific helpers such as `normpdf` remain available.
